answer: Register one willow coppice per applicant on a surveyed knoll above shale ground for 120 days, with a 150 token deposit and an 85 dollar license. The keeper tags 30 willow stools with numbered steel bands, cuts each stool each season, and weighs the bundled rods at a scale while a neighbor signs the tally. A forged tally forfeits the deposit and bars the keeper for 180 days. Faking 10,000 coppices freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 850,000 dollars in licenses. A coppice is like a ledger that grows back only where it was planted, so a fake plot has no roots to show when the inspector digs.
